E.g., 1) Add full X-band link budget in 2.4 including EIRP, G/T, path loss, modulation/coding, Eb/N0 margin, and verify Mount Pleasant 12 m antenna can support S/X-band fit-out or propose alternative. 2) Replace fixed 60% contact-time assumption in Table 6 with elevation-dependent pass modelling/scheduling, and quantify data throughput. 3) Address launch/revisit uncertainties: justify Vega C/rideshare dispersion and propulsion-free injection to 600 km/97.79°, and strengthen "any reef within five days" with latitude/daylight/cloud coverage analysis. Could also mention references scholarly. But only 3 next steps.

Criteria feedback <=70 words each.

C1: You address mission, rationale, single-spacecraft justification, operator/customers in Section 1 with Australia focus and references. To reach full Accomplished, strengthen scholarly/peer-reviewed sourcing and tighten linkage between rationale and design requirements. (Don't say "next level" since already accomplished; say full marks.)

C2: Comprehensive design across 2.2-2.5 with STK evidence and hand checks; orbital/decay calcs sound. To move from 9 to 10, add full X-band link budget, substantiate Mount Pleasant S/X-band fit-out, replace fixed 60% contact assumption with elevation-dependent pass scheduling, and address Vega C/rideshare dispersion and revisit claim rigour.

C3: Conclusions follow evidence, summarise key performance, identify four limitations and next steps. To reach full marks, tie each limitation explicitly to a design decision/requirement and quantify impact where possible.

C4: Clear structure, concise executive summary, labelled figures/tables, consistent citations matching bibliography. To reach full marks, polish minor presentation/reference-quality issues (e.g., ensure all sources are appropriate/scholarly and formatting fully consistent).
